What's up with Cecil the lion?

Cecil was a lion living in an animal reserve in Zimbabwe. It was tagged by scientist in 2009 (if I'm not mistaken), with a GPS activated collar, and studied by them since then. Because of its interactions with humans, it grew a bit less fearful of them, so many people could get as close as 10 meters (about 32 feet) from it to take pictures. With the years, it became almost like a mascot of the reserve, people coming to see it from far away countries.

Then, the American dentist paid a professional Zimbabwean hunter 55 k$ to hunt a lion. The hunter attracted a lion (certainly didn't know it was Cecil) out of the reserve for the American to hunt. The guy shot the lion with a crossbow, tracked it for a few hours and finished it off with a rifle, beheaded it to take its head back home as a trophy and left the rest of the carcass to rot there. After a few weeks the scientists having no news of the lion went looking for it, and finally found what was left of its corpse and that's when we started to hear about it.

As of today, it's not entirely clear at what point the American and the Zimbabwean hunters acted legally. They claimed so, having obtained a legal permit to hunt a lion, but Cecil was living on an animal reserve and was lured out of it. And the man on whose property Cecil was killed didn't have the legal quota to have a lion killed on his land. The American got his address and phone number leaked online and he got harassed. The Zimbabwean hunter was supposed to start his trial this week to find out the truth about all that.

A few airlines have banned the transport of hunting trophies to America and Europe. International organisations consider giving the lion an official endangered species status. A few petitions have been launched to either prosecute the American or the Zimbabwean hunter, to ask airlines to ban the transport of trophies, and all sorts of things about that situation.

And since animal cruelty is a fashionable cause to oppose, many celebrities have talked about it and many people not understanding what's happening in the world have parroted their favorite stars without much nuance.
